label: L16 · Microbes in Food
rows: Three effects
BENEFICIAL (fermentation improves flavor, taste, texture) · DETRIMENTAL (poisoning, intoxication, illness, spoilage) · NEUTRAL (just there, eaten with the food).
Bread
Leavening (carbon dioxide) · flavor and aroma (organic acids, alcohols) · conditioning (enzymes on gluten). Saccharomyces cerevisiae; some Clostridium; Lactobacillus sanfrancisco (sourdough).
Beer and wine

Glucose + yeast → 2 ethanol + 2 carbon dioxide. Brewing since 6000 BCE; malting, mashing, wort + hops, lagering, filtration. Wine from grapes or other fruit. Yeast source can be human SALIVA (chewed plant material).
Pickling, soy
Salt brine, lactic acid, vinegar, spices; soybeans → tofu, soy sauce; fish sauce, mole, tea, coffee.
Milk

STERILE until it exits the mammal; microbes from the body and milking UTENSILS; nutrient dense. First fermented dairy = accidental skin/nose/mouth microbes. Cheese: yeast, bacteria, molds. Yogurt: Lactobacillus + Streptococcus; kefir, koumiss, buttermilk.
Microbes as food
Spirulina (a cyanobacterium) in smoothies and gummies; single cell protein researched; feed additives already used for animals.
Fungi in food
Rarely cause disease; mushrooms, PENICILLIN, yeast fermentation; spoil bread, cereals, acidic juices.

label: L16 · The Problem & the First Split
rows: Scale
~250 foodborne pathogens; BACTERIA most common; also viruses, parasites, microbial toxins; under-reported (slide figures: 75 million cases, 5000+ deaths).
Who watches

Surveillance + outbreak investigation: local/state health departments, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Food and Drug Administration, United States Department of Agriculture. ENFORCEMENT and policy: Food and Drug Administration + United States Department of Agriculture.
Symptoms
Diarrhea, abdominal cramps, nausea, fever, vomiting.
Intoxication
PREFORMED TOXIN eaten → target organs. Staphylococcal toxin, Clostridium botulinum toxin.
Infection
LIVE CELLS eaten; improper cooking lets them MULTIPLY in the food → intestinal infection. Salmonella, Listeria.
The seven bacteria
E. coli, Salmonella, Campylobacter jejuni, Listeria monocytogenes, Clostridium, Bacillus cereus, Vibrio.

label: L16 · E. coli, Salmonella, Campylobacter
rows: Escherichia coli

FECAL INDICATOR organism (human and animal feces); EMB (eosin methylene blue) plates confirm it in food and water; not always pathogenic; toxin strains (enterotoxigenic, enterohemorrhagic); O157:H7 among the worst.
E. coli outbreaks
Fecally contaminated MEATS or VEGETABLES: hamburgers, bagged spinach, romaine lettuce, cookie dough, ground beef, raw milk cheese (western United States, 2026).
Salmonella
Animals, mainly POULTRY and AQUATIC REPTILES; gastroenteritis, enteric fever, septicemia, shock, kidney dysfunction; incubation HOURS to WEEKS; young children and the elderly at greatest risk.
Typhoid fever
Salmonella typhi: the MOST SEVERE enteric fever; invades the intestinal wall → blood and lymph nodes. 'Typhoid Mary' (Mary Mallon), the cook who persisted.
Salmonella sources
Poultry, EGGS, PET FOOD, live backyard poultry, PEANUT BUTTER, sushi-grade seafood; produce recalls (watermelon, onions, cantaloupe, cucumbers, jalapenos).
Campylobacter jejuni

A LEADING cause of bacterial diarrhea in the United States, esp. children; rapid fever, headache, dizziness, BLOODY diarrhea; infectious dose <500 cells (ONE DROP of raw poultry fluid); under-reported.

label: L16 · Listeria, Clostridium, B. cereus, Vibrio
rows: Listeria monocytogenes

Birds, mammals, SOIL; big recalls (ice cream, cantaloupe, frozen vegetables); PREGNANT women, unborn and premature babies, elderly, immunocompromised; slide: #1 cause of food-related DEATHS in the United States.
Listeria foods
Soft cheeses, deli meats, hot dogs, raw produce, raw meat, smoked seafood. Grows from 1 to 40 °C: FRIDGE, room and freezer temperatures. Spreads to brain and across the placenta to the fetus.
Clostridium
Gram-positive rods, STRICT ANAEROBES, SPORES (soil, plants, HONEY). Food: botulinum, perfringens. Not food: tetani, difficile.
Botulism
Toxin made when spores GERMINATE; foodborne and wound botulism; paralysis with muscles RELAXED → respiratory failure; a few bacteria make plenty of toxin.
Bacillus cereus
Very common, SUMMER; DIARRHEAL (meat) or EMETIC (rice); onset ≤6 hours; self-resolving vomiting and cramps; hot foods hot, cold foods cold.
Vibrio
cholerae, vulnificus, parahaemolyticus; SALT-tolerant, ocean and estuarine water; WATER (ingested, WOUNDS) or FOOD (shellfish, oysters, crabs, raw seafood); the R-month rule is now uncertain.

label: L16 · Protozoa, Worms, Viruses
rows: Protozoa
Cryptosporidium, Cyclospora, Giardia, Entamoeba: mild, self-limiting diarrhea from uncooked fruit and vegetables or DRINKING WATER; ready-to-eat SALAD BAGS.
Worms
Tapeworm, roundworm, trichinosis: killed by THOROUGH COOKING; venison and pork infected while the animal is ALIVE; pet feces.
Norovirus
Norwalk-like, Caliciviridae; person to person by FECES and VOMITUS (daycares, nursing homes, CRUISE SHIPS); shellfish; a FEW particles infect; rapid onset, short course.
Hepatitis A and E
FECAL-ORAL; most contagious ~2 WEEKS BEFORE symptoms; NOT kissing, sneezing, saliva or blood; vaccine after suspected exposure; handwashing, diaper hygiene.

label: L16 · Tracking, Objective 3, Prevention
rows: PulseNet

Each isolate's PULSED-FIELD GEL ELECTROPHORESIS pattern → the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention database. Finds outbreak causes and processing-plant problems; cuts DETECTION TIME and NUMBER OF CASES.
Matching patterns
The slide 34 gel: patient, environmental and animal E. coli O157 isolates share one pattern.
Recall sources
Food and Drug Administration (food, dietary supplements, PET FOOD) · United States Department of Agriculture · Foodsafetynews.com, Foodsafetymagazine.com.
Objective 3
Antibiotic resistance in the food supply: NO SLIDE covers it. Not quizzed; listen for it in the recording.
What you can do
Hot soapy handwashing · wash produce · when in doubt, toss it out · mild bleach on surfaces · meat thermometer 165 °F · no cross-contamination of boards · gloves, hair coverings · ServSafe.
